e6c2558dd35f707f4d1cc8ec4285d49c74e612aa.summary: A 2015 TrendLabs blog post by Trend Micro senior threat researcher David Sancho describes how malware uses steganography to hide code and command-and-control (C&C) traffic. It cites a DarkComet dropper, seen in November 2014, that hides encrypted code in a bitmap image in its resources. It describes the Morto Trojan sending Base64-encoded C&C commands in DNS responses, the TDSS/Alureon botnet fetching JPG images from popular blogging sites with commands hidden inside, and ShadyRAT hiding commands in HTML comments and in JPG files using LSB encoding.
